successCriteria.description: AuditLog entity is defined and exported from `src/modules/audit/audit.model.ts` with all canonical fields: id (string), entityType (string), entityId (string), action (string), oldValues (Record<string, unknown> | null), newValues (Record<string, unknown> | null), performedBy (string), performedAt (Date)

IAuditRepository interface declares create(entry: Omit<AuditLog, 'id' | 'performedAt'>): Promise<AuditLog>, findByEntity(entityType: string, entityId: string): Promise<AuditLog[]>, and findByPerformer(performedBy: string, limit?: number): Promise<AuditLog[]>
AuditRepository implements IAuditRepository using the shared pool from `src/shared/db/connection.ts`, targeting the `audit_logs` table with parameterized SQL and snake_case column mapping
AuditService.log(entry) auto-sets performedAt to new Date(), delegates to IAuditRepository.create, and returns the created AuditLog
AuditService.getEntityHistory(entityType, entityId) returns all AuditLog records for that entity, ordered by performedAt descending
AuditService.getUserActions(performedBy, limit?) returns AuditLog records for that performer, ordered by performedAt descending, capped at limit when provided

Notification entity is defined and exported from `src/modules/notification/notification.model.ts` with all canonical fields: id (string), recipientId (string), title (string), body (string), type ('EMAIL' | 'IN_APP'), isRead (boolean), metadata (Record<string, unknown> | null), createdAt (Date)

INotificationRepository interface declares create(notification: Omit<Notification, 'id' | 'createdAt' | 'isRead'>): Promise<Notification>, findByRecipient(recipientId: string, limit?: number): Promise<Notification[]>, and markAsRead(id: string): Promise<void>

NotificationRepository implements INotificationRepository using the shared pool from `src/shared/db/connection.ts`, targeting the `notifications` table with parameterized SQL and snake_case column mapping

NotificationService.send(recipientId, title, body, type, metadata?) creates a Notification with isRead=false and createdAt=now, delegates to INotificationRepository.create, and returns the created Notification
NotificationService.getForUser(recipientId, limit?) returns notifications for that recipient ordered by createdAt descending, capped at limit when provided
NotificationService.markRead(id) delegates to INotificationRepository.markAsRead; throws a typed domain error (e.g. NotificationNotFoundError) if the notification does not exist

constraints: No use of `any` — use `unknown` with type guards (HARNESS.json constraint no-any)
All database access must go through the repository pattern — no inline SQL in services (GP-001, HARNESS.json no-direct-db-outside-repository)
No hardcoded secrets, passwords, API keys, or tokens (HARNESS.json no-hardcoded-secrets)

entityInvariants.invariant: AuditLog records are immutable once created — no update or delete operations exist on the repository or service
The `action` field must be constrained to values from the `AuditAction` enum defined in `src/shared/types/leave.types.ts`
A newly created Notification always has isRead=false and createdAt set to the current timestamp at creation time
The `type` field must be exactly 'EMAIL' or 'IN_APP' — no other values are valid

interfaceConstraints.errorSemantics: Must throw a typed domain error if the repository create fails (e.g. database constraint violation); must not silently swallow errors
Must throw a typed domain error (e.g. NotificationNotFoundError) if no notification with the given id exists; calling markRead on an already-read notification is a no-op (idempotent)
Must throw a typed domain error if type is not 'EMAIL' or 'IN_APP'; must throw if title or body is empty

consistencyRequirements.requirement: AuditLog.action must be validated against the AuditAction enum values from `src/shared/types/leave.types.ts`

Repository implementations must follow the established pattern from EmployeeRepository and PolicyRepository: private mapRow method converting snake_case DB columns to camelCase entity fields, parameterized SQL with $1/$2 placeholders, RETURNING * on INSERT, and dynamic UPDATE with a fieldMap array
Service classes must follow the constructor-injection pattern: accept the repository interface as a constructor parameter, never instantiate the repository internally
